# Breadcrumb

The trail from the top of the site to the current page: a labelled `<nav>` with an ordered list of links, the last item marked `aria-current="page"`. A long trail keeps its first and last steps and collapses the middle into a `Menu`.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/breadcrumb/breadcrumb";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { label: "Home", href: "/" },
    { label: "Recipes", href: "/recipes" },
    { label: "Short ribs" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Navbar` or `Sidebar` instead for the app's main sections, and `Tabs` for views of one page.

## Props

Type: `BreadcrumbProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mb-4`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | The text of the item that closes the hidden steps' sheet on a phone. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly BreadcrumbItem[]` |  | The trail from the top of the site to the current page, which is the last item. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Breadcrumb"` | Names the navigation for screen readers. |
| `maxItems` | `number` | `4` | The longest trail shown in full. A longer one keeps the first item and the last ones (`maxItems - 2` of them, at least the current page) and puts the middle in a menu, which is a bottom sheet below 640px. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `"More"` | The name of the "…" button that opens the hidden steps. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `children`: Not rendered. The trail is data: `<Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "Home", href: "/" }, { label: "Ribs" }]} />`.
- `links`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `items`: `<Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "Home", href: "/" }, { label: "Ribs" }]} />`.
- `separator`: Not a prop. Breadcrumb draws its own separators.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `BreadcrumbItem`

One step of a Breadcrumb's trail.

```ts
interface BreadcrumbItem {
  /** The page's name: "Recipes". */
  label: string;
  /**
   * Where the step goes; internal paths go through `OuroProvider`'s `linkComponent`. Every
   * item needs one except the last, the current page, which renders as text.
   */
  href?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * An icon before the label, as an element: `icon: <HomeIcon />`. It is hidden from
   * screen readers, so the label still names the step.
   */
  icon?: ReactNode;
}
```
